name: Lit Sill Line
tagline: The family's week as a signal box's lit track diagram, the greeting standing on its own Coming up line: the tube is the first stop, the airglow rises off the lit run, the family's hand is ink, and Status's lamps are typed on the glass.
concept: Branch Lines drew every boxed page from its own data but left Home as its parent's; this graft makes Home the diagram's terminus, and carries the same line on to Plans. The greeting is a lit board whose foot is the Coming up rail itself: the lamp that means now breathes at its left end, the run from it is lit as far as the first stop, which is the Next up tube (its power lamp drops a lit wire to the rail), the later plans are stops along the same rail with their days in the glass and their plates hanging below, and the rail ends at a buffer. The greeting's old green pool is explained as airglow rising off that lit run. 'Now, a lit run to the next stop' is one rule on Home, To do, the Plans list and the month. Around it a second rule holds on every page: the machine's words and marks are phosphor, the board and its rails are slate and steel, and what the family wrote or put on the calendar is ink.
companions: Ink is the companion with a job. What the family wrote or put on the calendar sits on a midnight #182536 plate with a #2e4460 edge and a pale #86a9cc cap or bar: their chat plates, Coming up's plates under the sill, the Plans list's plan names, and the month's plans. Every field they type in is a #0d141c well with a #56708c edge. Ink is never used on a board, a row or text. The board keeps steel: #58697a rails, #7d8fa0 buffers and drops, #a7c4d8 links and the #26313a latched cell for 'here'. Cyan #70dcf4 marks a plan's ring. Amber is only for late and the setup edge. Sage #86d9a6 is the word 'now', a done tick and the row afterglow. The kind rings are grounded: terracotta #df987c for restaurants, moss #b5c87d for outings and wheat #c3a85d for seasonal ideas. #6dff9c is lit only where something is live: the mark, 'planning', Send, the box, focus, the now lamps and their runs, working lamps and the tubes.
decisions: Built as a clean sheet, as this round's refinement also is: today's stylesheet themed by the harness's own theme.py from these tokens, then the lineage's sources in their order (track.css, phosphor.css, relight.css, branch.css) and this graft's sill.css, built by src/build.py. The brief asked to pay for the graft inside the 60K css budget; the sheet gives the room, and the dead rules the brief named (the shelf and its well, the Coming up tray, the backlit key, the week rails) were deleted anyway.

A (L099 and L098), the greeting on its line. From 64rem the board is [Next up tube 23rem | question and box] inside the same 74rem page as every inner page. Vera's name and the day run across the top, so the tube's top and the box's top share one line, and the tube stands on the sill. The sill is the board's foot: a 2px steel rail drawn from the board's left edge to a real T buffer (a 2px by 14px bar across the rail) at the board's inner padding, where the plates end; past the buffer only the board's hairline. The now lamp breathes at its left end, with 'now' in 13px sage. The run from it is lit with a white-hot core as far as station one, where a lit wire drops from the tube's power lamp. Stations two to five are cyan rings under the question. Their days (30px Archivo 300, month and weekday stacked in 13px mono) stand above the rail in the glass, and their ink plates hang below the sill on 1px drops, about 170px each. Each day, ring and plate belong to one list item, so they cannot drift apart. 'All plans' sits under the plates on their right edge, below the buffer. Under the lit run stand 'Coming up' and the source note alone: the count is said once, by the tube's '4 more on the line'.

The airglow is L098/L099 rebuilt on the sill: .welcome::before 9rem tall from the sill, the green rising, masked at 18% where the lit run's middle is, with E7's whisper of scanlines kept inside it; E7's pool from the lower left stays at 0.13; the sill spills 0 24px 40px -30px of green onto the plates; the cobalt corner stays off. It samples (36,64,45) over the lit run against (16,22,17) under the question and (15,22,16) in the top right corner. Under more contrast the airglow and the spill go.

The tube is a grid, not a float: 'NEXT UP' and the plan's name run across the glass, then when and '> 4 more on the line' down the left, with a 7.5rem scope in the foot band at the right. The name holds one line ('Silver Falls hike'), the date breaks after its comma ('Thursday 1 October, / 10:00 [TOMORROW]'), and the prompt with its cursor sits at the foot of the screen beside the scope, so no glass is left dead under a floated radar. On a phone the date runs the glass's width and the 5rem scope keeps to the foot band. The tube keeps .crt.next-up, screenGlow 1.0 and the 3px graphite case.

D. The route sets on opening: an aria-hidden span.roll in the crt macro rolls a 2px white-hot line with a 14px bloom and a faint wake down every tube once (1.25s after 0.15s), which the motion-on frames at 220, 450 and 900ms catch; on Home a white-hot head runs along the sill from the now lamp to the first stop over 0.9s, opening the lit run behind it, and the airglow fades up after. Nothing loops; under reduced motion all of it is lit at once. Found on the way: an animation whose name a media query changes starts again during the harness's full-page capture, so the run across (desktop) and the run down (phone) share one keyframe.

B (L004), ink, in Late Set's midnight form, with the brief's tokens except one: the well's edge is #56708c, not #34485e. #34485e measures only 1.97:1 on the well, and a field's edge should reach 3:1; #56708c gives 3.6:1. The plate's chroma is 0.037, a hair over the brief's 0.035 and far from Tokyo Night's #7aa2f7. Home's box stays on the greeting's glass. The Plans list is the sill continued: the rows stay slate on the steel rail with cyan rings and the lit now lamp at the top of the run, and each plan's name is an ink plate with the 2px cap (faded ink for 'Recently'), its ring set at the plate's middle. The phone's month list takes the same plates.

C (L253), Status as one instrument. The spend tube is 30rem wide. Under a dim rule on its glass sit three 44px lamp strings, each a link to its board, such as 'WHO ANSWERS ● ● ● ○ 3 OF 4'. Each is read out in full ('Who answers 3 of 4 working'). The lamps are 16px, 0.75rem apart, in the tube's own strengths: a white-hot core in a halo (working), an 8px dim dot (waiting), a 2px dim ring (off) and a 2px dashed dim ring (not set up), so the four read apart without the legend. Pointed at or focused, a string goes inverse. Beside the tube, the tally doubles as the legend, so each count is said once: each figure is 40px Archivo next to the page lamp it counts (6 working, 1 waiting, 2 off, 4 not set up), then '0 partly working · 0 stopped'. 'Change the limit' is the tube's caption. Each board's head carries its count ('3 of 4'). Who answers stays lit lamp to lamp, and the fallback that cannot take over turns off through a 45° turnout into a buffer.

E. The lineage's fixes: 'here' is the #26313a latched cell with a 2px steel cap (a ring lamp on the bar's rule) in the bar, the phone's tabs, the keys, the tabs and the settings nav, and today's cell on the month keeps the latched fill and cap under its now lamp; the question is 40px Archivo 700 at 78% width with 'planning' in E1's two layers; setup keeps its line across with hollow amber rings, the next one rimmed in the phosphor and named 'Next step', each action run in bold, the rail ending at a buffer beside 'All the setup steps'; Chat's 'Vera' stands flush left with its lede under it, the rails are 18px apart and begin at the day's tie, each time is printed once on the spine, only the newest stop (her screen, her words, its time) is lit, and 'your turn' names the ring on the box; the kind rings are terracotta, moss and wheat with the kind words in ink-2; the row afterglow is a 2px sage edge with a short halo and a faint wash, on in 0.12s and held before it fades over 1.2s; nothing a person reads is under 13px and no target is under 44px on any rendered page.

Ideas' line from home: home, a short stub and one 45° jog, then a log scale from 15 minutes. Stations are ticks. Only three are named, by number, name and drive alone ('#7 Pumpkin patch at Bi-Mart farm · 18 min'): the compass is left to the Drive column, since VT323 at 18px under the scanlines drew 'NW' as a smudge. The :has() rules cover 40 rows. The Drive column pads minutes after hours ('2 h 05 min'), so its figures line up.

Plans, the month: the week that holds today carries the line, as Home's sill does. A 2px rail runs under the days from the now lamp in today's cell (lit, not breathing, under the date, with 'now' in 13px sage beside '30') to a T buffer at Sunday's end. The run from the lamp is lit with the hot core as far as the next plan's cyan ring (Silver Falls, Thu 1). Each later plan in that week hangs from its ring on the rail by a 1px drop, its ink plate below, so day, ring and plate stand as they do on Home. Today keeps the #26313a latched fill with its steel cap. The other weeks keep their plates with a small ring inside; weeks gone by with nothing in them fold to a single line. The month's head says what it counts: '2 coming by Sun 4 Oct / next tomorrow 10:00', since the month page only knows its own days. The Plans list's head now matches Home's count: '5 coming / next tomorrow 10:00'.

The kids' wishes are one 44px line at the foot of To do ('The kids' wishes · Maya 0 open · Theo 0 open · All'); what waits on a parent still comes first. The top wishes each kid's row used to show are not on the line.

'now' is the sage word beside a lit lamp on every timetable: Home's sill, To do, the Plans list and the month's line (setup's 'Next step' is the sage word beside a phosphor ring). It is never a second glowing word, so the only lit word on Home is the job, 'planning'.
title: What are we *planning*? The household's own present tense: it asks what the family has on the go and invites them to tell Vera, and on this Home the lit line of plans the question stands on answers it directly below. The lit word is the job, not the motif; it avoids 'next', which the tube's NEXT UP claims beside it, and 'shall', which the judges found stiff. At 21 characters it holds one line at 40px on the desktop and at about 29px on a phone, and as the box's label it tells a first-time user what the box is for.
strengths: Home changes above the fold and in its content. The greeting and Coming up are one lit board standing on its own line. The tube is the first stop, with its power lamp wired to the rail, and the four later plans hang from the sill with their days in the glass. The rail ends at a real T buffer where the plates end.

'Now, a lit run to the next stop' is now one rule on four pages: Home's sill, To do's timetable, the Plans list and the month, where the week that holds today carries the line and its plans hang from rings as Home's do.

The phosphor's light is back on live data, not spread across the page. The now lamp breathes, the occupied run is white-hot, the airglow rises off it and fades up once it is set, and every tube rolls a line of light once as it switches on.

One rule gives colour a job on every page: phosphor for the machine, slate and steel for the board, ink for the family's hand. Chat's green share falls from 97.5% to 48.8% and Status's from 99.3% to about 70%. The Plans list's plan names are ink plates on the steel rail.

Status reads without the list. Each group's lamps are named and counted on the glass, drawn at 16px so working, waiting, off and not set up read apart, and each string links to its board. Every count on the page is said once, beside the lamp it counts.
The Next up tube is a grid: the plan's name on one line, the date broken at its comma, the prompt and cursor at the screen's foot beside the scope, and no dead glass under a floated radar.

Typesetting: a 13px floor, a 40px condensed question, light 30px day numerals stacked with mono month and weekday, balanced plate titles, tabular figures padded where they should align ('2 h 05 min'), counts that agree between Home and the Plans list, and sentence case everywhere off the glass. There are 0 targets under 44px on every rendered page, on desktop and phone.
weaknesses: It is still a line-heavy design, and the month now carries a line too. A judge who reads lines as a subway map will find one on every page.

'All plans' sits under the plates at their right edge, about 40px below the buffer it belongs to. It does not stand beside the buffer, as setup's 'All the setup steps' does, because the four plates fill the rail up to the buffer.
The sill draws at most four stops after Next up (coming[1:5]). With fewer plans the rail runs on empty to the buffer, and on a busy fortnight the fifth and later plans are only behind 'All plans'.

The month still opens on four folded weeks gone by (about 160px) before the week that holds today, and its head says '2 coming by Sun 4 Oct' where the list says '5 coming': both are true, but the family sees two numbers.

Several things are worked out in the templates from a row's words or the app's clock: the lamp states on Status and Settings, the month's line classes and its head, the Plans list's 'next' words, Ideas' drive and scale, and the kids' line. Each should become a small field in views.py when it ships.

On a phone the tube's foot band is the 5rem scope's height, so about 40px of glass stands empty to the left of it, above the prompt. The phone's month plates wrap in their narrow column ('Silver Falls / hike 10:00').
Status leaves about 160px of slate to the right of the tally at 1280.

The page's words move: Ideas' differ from today's by 33.1% (the line from home's words), To do's by 20.9% (the head's figure, the column heads, and 'Edit' in place of the disclosure's longer label), Home's by 12.5% and Status's by 9.5%.
revisions: Plans, the month (the critic's first fix): the week that holds today carries the line again. The lit now lamp (not breathing) replaces the steel ring by the date, with 'now' in 13px sage beside '30'. A 2px steel rail runs from it to a T buffer at Sunday's end. The run to Silver Falls' cyan ring is lit with the hot core, and later plans in that week hang from rings on 1px drops. The latched fill stays. One change from the note: the rail runs under the days, not along the row's foot. That way the lamp, the lit run and the ring are on one line, and the plates hang from it as they do from Home's sill, where a foot rail would pass under the plates it serves.

Home, the Next up tube: the float and shape-outside are replaced by a grid (areas label / title / when + radar / more + radar, with .next-text as display: contents, the radar at align-self: end, and the row gap taken out so the free glass goes to the foot band). 'Silver Falls hike' now holds one line and the date breaks after 'October,'. On a phone the date runs the glass's width and the scope is 5rem.
Home, the width: the 80rem main is gone, so Home keeps the 74rem page edge of every inner page. The tube is 23rem, and the plates keep about 170px each.
Home, the Coming up head: the '4 / more after Next up' figure is deleted. 'Coming up' and the source note stand alone under the lit run, and the tube's '4 more on the line' says the count once.

Home, the rail's end: the buffer is a real T, a 2px by 14px steel bar across the rail at the board's inner padding. The rail is drawn only as far as the buffer, with the board's hairline beyond it. 'All plans' leaves the days row and sits under the plates, right-aligned on their edge. The note asked for it beside the buffer, but the plates fill the rail up to the buffer, so there is no room for it there without narrowing them. On a phone the vertical line still ends in its buffer beside 'All plans'.
Status, the glass lamps: 16px, a 2px dashed ring for 'not set up', an 8px waiting dot, and 0.75rem between lamps. CONNECTED's five states now read apart without the legend.

Ideas, the line from home: the compass is dropped from the named stations ('#7 Pumpkin patch at Bi-Mart farm · 18 min') and left to the Drive column. The Drive column also pads minutes after hours ('2 h 05 min'), the type lens's older note.

The Plans list: rendered and made the sill continued. The rows stay slate on the steel rail with cyan rings and the lit now lamp at the head of the run, and each plan's name is an ink plate with the 2px #86a9cc cap, its ring at the plate's middle ('Recently' in faded ink). Its head now agrees with Home: '5 coming / next tomorrow 10:00'. The month's head says what it counts ('2 coming by Sun 4 Oct'). The phone's month list takes the same plates, and today's stamp there is sage, not phosphor.

None of the notes was declined outright. Two were adapted, as said above: the month's rail runs under the days rather than along the row's foot, and 'All plans' sits under the plates rather than beside the buffer. I looked at every page again after the changes (home, home-phone, chat, chat-phone, ideas, plans, the Plans list, todo, status, settings, general and form), plus the motion frames and a reduced-motion Home.
